item.title: US-led Gaza peace board warns Hamas over kites after Israeli threat
item.description: The US-led board overseeing the Gaza peace plan warned Hamas on Tuesday to halt militant activity, including flying kites, after Israel threatened retaliatory strikes. A Board of Peace official said Israel must also respect the ceasefire, limiting military action to responses to “genuine and imminent threats.”

item.title: Despite ceasefire, Israeli strikes still kill in Gaza and the West Bank
item.description: Despite a ceasefire that has been in place since October 2025, violence continues in Gaza. On August 23, Israeli strikes left several people dead in the enclave, and a young boy was killed by the Israeli military in the West Bank, according to local authorities. Since the announcement of the truce, more than 1,280 Palestinians have been killed in Gaza, while Israel has reported the launch of drones, balloons and kites towards its territory.

item.title: Israel's Netanyahu says Iran tried to assassinate one of his sons
item.description: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said on Monday that Iran had attempted to assassinate one of his two sons, without providing evidence or further details. “Iran tried to kill one of my sons,” Netanyahu told Israel’s Channel 14, as he discussed security arrangements ahead of the October 27 election.

item.title: France and Saudi Arabia hold talks ranging from Middle East to esports
item.description: Mohammed bin Salman has arrived in Paris for a two-day official visit with French President Emmanuel Macron. Talks are expected to include the war in Iran and the Strait of Hormuz, as well as new energy routes to bypass the Strait. The two made an appearance at the closing ceremony of the Esports World Cup, held for the first time outside of Saudi Arabia but largely funded by Riyadh.

item.title: Iran offers $10 million to kill Trump's son
item.description: Iranian state media has aired a video that appears to threaten the life of Barron Trump, US President Donald Trump's youngest son. Since the start of the war in February, Iranian media have on multiple occasions circulated content threatening the president and family members. The US Secret Service has confirmed it is aware of the video.

item.title: US economic D-Day sanctions: 'Repeated bombing attacks across Iran failed to change the calculus'
item.description: Genie Godula is pleased to welcome Imran Bayoumi, Deputy Director & Resident Fellow at the Atlantic Council. He sees the Trump administration’s new sanctions strategy toward Iran as an attempt to seek economic leverage where military force has so far failed to produce any results. But its effectiveness rests on several unresolved assumptions. item.title: With sanctions and tariffs, US bets on its economic power to get what it wants
item.description: The US has announced a new wave of sanctions on Iran and has promised to sanction any countries trading with it - including China. It also comes as the US deepens a trade war with its neighbour Canada. FRANCE 24's Kethevane Gorjestani tells us more.

item.title: Mideast live: Oil tanker struck by projectile in Strait of Hormuz off Oman
item.description: President ​Donald Trump on Tuesday said all ​mines ‌within ⁠the ‌international waters of ⁠the Strait of Hormuz ​had been ‌removed or detonated, ‌and that ​Iran had been notified that any ship ​or ​boat ​placing new ​mines would be destroyed under a US “zero tolerance policy”. Read our blog to see how the day's events unfolded.

item.title: MBS in the City of Light: In a world of realpolitik, does West value economic interests over values?
item.description: Jean-Emile Jammine is pleased to welcome Susanne Koelbl, Der Spiegel's award-winning foreign correspondent. According to Koelbl,, Emmanuel Macron’s decision to welcome Mohammed bin Salman at the Élysée reflects realpolitik in its purest form: 'Saudi Arabia had become too important for energy, regional security, investment and diplomacy in the Middle East to be permanently isolated. So Macron wanted to establish France as an independent, balanced power between the Mediterranean and the Gulf."

item.title: Middle East live: Iran warns of a harsh response to anticipated US sanctions
item.description: Iranian Economy Minister Ali Madanizadeh on Monday warned of "another defeat" for the US after Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent announced expanded sanctions against Tehran. Madanizadeh said Iran had a "two-year plan" to counter the new sanctions and dismissed Bessent's stated efforts to sever "every economic lifeline" sustaining Iran. Read our blog to see how the day's events unfolded.
